atlas-sa.0130: Saudis made up 41% of new hires in Jisr’s 2025–2026 report, and Riyadh took more than half of all new hires; the World Bank counts 35.8% of Saudis with tertiary education in 2025 against 24.4% of expatriates.
atlas-sa.0132: Apply through the Study in Saudi portal: a long-term educational visa for a full degree, with a student iqama sponsored by the university; a short-term one for language courses and exchanges up to a year.
atlas-sa.0133: Students may not work off campus at all; only paid research or teaching assistant roles at the university.
atlas-sa.0134: SAR 800, or free with a scholarship
atlas-sa.0135: Research internships and temporary work visas
atlas-sa.0136: There is no internship visa. KAUST’s Visiting Student Research Program takes STEM students for 3 to 6 months with a stipend, housing and the visa paid; a company hosting a graduate must sponsor a temporary work visa. Internships on a tourist or business visa lead to expulsion.
atlas-sa.0139: Temporary work visa, paid by the company
atlas-sa.0141: There is no job-search visa. A graduate who signs with an employer on Qiwa before the student iqama ends can transfer sponsorship without leaving; otherwise the university issues a final exit.
atlas-sa.0143: The employer allocates a visa on Qiwa, you accept the electronic contract, and the visa is issued at a Tasheer centre; the iqama follows within 90 days of arrival. There is no income tax on salaries.
atlas-sa.0144: The employer pays the visa, the yearly expat levy and the iqama; you pay for dependants. Some fields reserve 40% to 70% of roles for Saudis, and foreign engineers need five years of experience to register.
atlas-sa.0149: No change of employer in the first 12 months unless the employer fails to pay or to issue the iqama.
atlas-sa.0151: Residence with no sponsor for five years, free to change jobs, without the expat or dependant levies; permanent after 30 months of actual stay.
atlas-sa.0157: Every KAUST master’s and PhD student gets a fellowship: no tuition, free campus housing and health cover, and a yearly allowance.
atlas-sa.0158: Research stays up to six months need a host invitation and a short-term educational visa; a tourist visa does not give lab access.
atlas-sa.0161: Saudi Arabia has no working-holiday agreements; working on a tourist visa is a crime.
atlas-sa.0162: EU and UK citizens get a one-year multiple-entry eVisa or a visa on arrival, up to 90 days a visit, with no work or internships.
atlas-sa.0164: Check and accept your contract on Qiwa, do the medical screening (Tasheer from Italy, Wafid elsewhere), apostille your degrees and a criminal record no older than 3 to 6 months, and collect the work visa sticker at a Tasheer centre.
atlas-sa.0165: Within the first 30 days, register your National Address with Saudi Post (SPL). Leases are signed digitally on the government platform Ejar, which needs your residence permit (iqama) and Nafath login.
atlas-sa.0166: At the border you get a 10-digit border number; within 90 days of entry your employer must pay the expat levy (SAR 9,600) and the iqama fee (SAR 650) and issue your iqama on Muqeem.
atlas-sa.0167: On a single-entry work visa, do not leave before the iqama is issued: the visa lapses at the border and the whole process starts again from abroad.
atlas-sa.0168: Once you have the iqama, move your SIM from the border number to it, activate Absher at a self-service kiosk, and set up Nafath, the face-recognition login for government services and banks.
atlas-sa.0169: Within 30 days, have the local medical check, uploaded to the Efada system (SAR 150 to 300); your employer activates your health insurance with the Council of Health Insurance.
atlas-sa.0170: A payroll account at a Saudi bank (SNB, Al Rajhi, Riyad Bank, SAB) needs an active iqama, the National Address and Nafath: with the border number alone you cannot open one.
atlas-sa.0171: To travel abroad with an iqama you need an active exit and re-entry visa on Absher; leaving without one, or coming back late, cancels the iqama and brings a 3-year ban on returning to work.
atlas-sa.0172: Before the iqama is issued you cannot leave: the single-entry work visa lapses at the border. Afterwards every trip needs an exit and re-entry visa on Absher.
atlas-sa.0173: A positive test for HIV, hepatitis B or C, syphilis or TB scarring in the local medical means deportation and a ban across the Gulf.
atlas-sa.0174: Resign before two years and you get no end-of-service award.
atlas-sa.0175: Italians who do not register with AIRE within 90 days remain tax residents in Italy, which then taxes the Saudi salary.
atlas-sa.0176: Foreigners pay no Saudi pension contributions, and there is no pension agreement with Italy: those years are a gap.
atlas-sa.0177: Most Saudi fees were not re-checked against official tables in the latest review.
atlas-sa.0178: Temporary bank accounts on a border number exist on paper; in practice new hires wait 30 to 45 days for a salary account.
atlas-sa.0179: Compound housing in Riyadh is saturated by companies moving regional headquarters there.
